description.narrative: The overarching development objective of this program is to use contract monitoring approaches and tools to strengthen transparency and accountability frameworks in the procurement systems in Ghana, Liberia, Nigeria, and Sierra Leone. The program will develop the capacity of emerging national civil society coalitions to monitor and improve governance in their respective national public procurement/contracting systems. These coalitions will be linked through a regional coordinating body for this work, thereby strengthening their overall effectiveness through knowledge-sharing and peer support and learning. The development objective of this program is to build the capacity of emerging multi-stakeholder groups in Ghana, Liberia, Nigeria, and Sierra Leone to more effectively monitor procurement/contracting processes and outcomes. Specifically the program will support these emerging coalitions (comprised of civil society, government, and the private sector) to monitor the award and implementation of selected projects (to be determined by the coalitions) and to advocate for improved governance in priority sectors. The expected results of the program are: (i) improved transparency and accountability of procurement/contracting processes in priority sectors/projects; (ii) sustainable monitoring coalitions of diverse stakeholders in each of the four target countries that will continue to oversee contracting processes after the program ends; and (iii) a regional network of stakeholders across the four countries that is committed to move the agenda of contract monitoring forward on the regional level. To achieve these results, the program will work through the Ghana Anti-Corruption Coalition (the recipient of the IDF grant) to provide peer-coaching and learning in the four target countries on procurement/contract monitoring, strategic advocacy, coalition and network building.
